articles.title: ‘Why do you never buy a round?!’ 20 mortifying money conversations with friends – and how to handle them
articles.summary: Whether it’s paying for dinner, going on holiday or sharing a taxi, friendships can be fraught with financial frustrations, which are very rarely aired. Here’s how to break the taboo. Summer is the season of socialising, from alfresco drinks to weddings to group holidays.
body: British pub etiquette seems simple: in a group of friends, everyone takes it in turns to buy the drinks. In practice, it is a minefield. There’s always someone who hangs back in the hope it won’t come round to them; someone who orders half a lager when it’s their turn to pay and a double G&T when it’s yours; couples who see themselves as one entity when it comes to paying, but not when it comes to drinking.

Ellie Austin-Williams, the London-based author of Money Talks: A Lifestyle Guide for Financial Wellbeing, says it is best to bring it up straight away. “Have the conversation at the start: do you want to do a round, or shall we pay our own way?” Isn’t that a bit embarrassing? “People feel it’s too awkward, but it’s better to say: ‘I’ll buy my own, I’m not drinking today.’ People really do respect that.” Conversely, if you’ve all agreed upfront to do rounds, it’s harder for someone to shirk their turn.

articles.title: Social media on trial as $200bn case against Facebook and Instagram begins
articles.summary: Twenty-nine US states are seeking huge damages, claiming Meta’s platforms were addictive by design. In 1994, more than 40 US states came together to sue one of the most powerful industries on Earth: big tobacco.
body: The suits brought together diverse claims centred on tobacco companies’ misleading advertising and contribution to a mounting public health crisis. They ended in a negotiated settlement with the US government, in which the companies agreed to pay more than any industry ever, and the states agreed to drop a large portion of their claims.
Thirty years later, smoking is on the rise in the developing world, the companies involved remain profitable and the global tobacco market is worth nearly $1tn.
On Tuesday a major trial against Meta began, in which 29 states have brought the claim that the parent of Facebook and Instagram designed a deliberately addictive product and targeted it at children.

That trial follows a bellwether case earlier this year, in which a Los Angeles jury found the social media company – and YouTube, its co-defendant – liable for deliberately designing an addictive product that had deleterious effects on the mental health of a single young claimant.

articles.title: ‘Audiences ask to feel my calves!’ The endurance extremists pounding treadmills and pumping pedals at the fringe
articles.summary: How do you keep audiences gripped while cycling 27km per show? From the Australian recreating a Tour de France win to a ‘toxically positive’ spin queen, we meet the acts bringing Olympian fitness to Edinburgh. Blood and sweat drip to the floor. Tears are on their way.
body: Across the city, Connor Delves’s calves are worth watching. The workout from his cycling-obsessed play, Cadel: Lungs on Legs, is so powerful that people have come up to him after, wanting to touch them. “To make sure they’re real,” says Delves, who cycles a whopping 27km per show. Does he mind this attention? He shrugs. “If they’re OK with getting their hands sweaty, go for it.”

Delves grew up in his parents’ bike shop in Perth, Western Australia. His mum was a triathlete, his dad an international mountain-biker. “It’s always been acting and sport for me,” he says. When he was replaced by a bigger name in a transferring show, he decided to make a production in which he was irreplaceable. “I’d never seen a play that showed endurance sport at its best,” he says, “where the sport is an actual effort.”

articles.title: I’m 50 years old. Why do I still struggle with the need to be liked?
articles.summary: An over-investment in people-pleasing can be emotionally costly. Here’s how I’m training myself to be OK with letting people down. A few months ago, my 10-year-old daughter and I went to our neighborhood cafe. At the counter, the owner greeted us with her typical effusion of warmth and welcome.
body: My face flushed. I was embarrassed and incensed by what I perceived as blatant rudeness. You could at least smile, I thought.

When we left, I pulled my daughter aside and gave her a firm talk about respect and manners, but her face dropped and she looked like she might cry. I quickly realized that she was in a bad mood, and totally unaware of her external affect. I felt bad for not approaching the conversation differently – I had assumed she recognized her impoliteness, that she was taking a stab at playing “sulky irreverent teen”.

That’s when it hit me: by dictating that she should comport herself contrary to how she was actually feeling, I was reinforcing society’s attempts to mold girls and women into automatons who reflexively try to please everyone but themselves. It’s ironic, because I had written an entire book to warn her about doing just that: Ugly: A Letter to My Daughter. I knew these types of messages often lead to what psychologist Mary Pipher writes about in Reviving Ophelia: a “split self” that often results in the creation of a “false self” in line with gendered expectations.

articles.title: Dior’s Mathilde Favier Has Died at 57
articles.summary: Mathilde Favier, Dior Couture’s longtime public relations director, died on Tuesday in a tragic accident, leaving a void in the world of fashion and culture.
body: This Tuesday, August 18, Mathilde Favier, Dior Couture’s longtime director of public relations, died in Airvault, France, in a car accident that also claimed the life of her husband, Nicolas Altmayer. Favier was 57 and Altmayer, a film producer, was 61.

The House of Dior remembered Favier as “an exceptional woman whose communicative joy, talent and loyalty were exemplary.” In a statement, Delphine Arnault, chairman and chief executive officer of Christian Dior Couture, added: “Mathilde loved life with a passion. With the passing of Mathilde, Dior is losing an incredible professional, and I have lost a loyal friend. Her optimism and courage commanded admiration. We will sorely miss her smile and her talent. I feel deeply saddened today; my thoughts are very much with her children, her mother, her sisters, her family, her many friends and her team she loved so much.”

Bernard Arnault also paid tribute to Favier, stating: “I was deeply saddened to learn of the tragic and sudden passing of Mathilde Favier, who devoted so many years to putting her passion, energy and talent at the service of the House of Dior. My heartfelt condolences go to her family and loved ones.”
points: Mathilde Favier, Dior Couture’s longtime public relations director, died on Tuesday in a tragic accident, leaving a void in the world of fashion and culture.

articles.summary: As the A-list prove, couples are increasingly saying “I do” to complementary ring designs. Vogue takes a closer look at the matching wedding band trend as spotted on Tom Holland and Zendaya.
body: In recent weeks, the internet has been abuzz with speculation that Gigi Hadid and Bradley Cooper have tied the knot, and that Zendaya and Tom Holland, who were legally married earlier this year, celebrated their nuptials for a second time, surrounded by family and friends, at Beaverbrook in Surrey.

As a result, all eyes have been on the matching “wedding” bands that have been sported by the two couples in London and Paris. Not long after news of their UK celebrations hit the press, Christopher Nolan’s Telemachus and Athena were spotted in the British capital looking low-key on a dog walk, wearing matching gold bands (Z’s East-West engagement ring by Jessica McCormack was also visible). While in the French capital, Hadid and Cooper were seen wearing coordinating neutral hues and complementary Boucheron bands.

articles.title: 6 Best Hair Gloss Treatments for At-Home Shine
articles.summary: Dull, lackluster hair? The best hair gloss treatments can restore shine in minutes, all from the comfort of your home. Shop our favorites, from Oribe to IGK.
body: If there’s anything I swear by, it’s a good hair gloss. I live and die by it because it’s one of the quickest ways I can delude myself into believing I have it “all together.” The rest of my life can deteriorate around me as long as my hair is shiny and healthy-looking enough to prompt a double-take—eliciting just the right amount of envy from whoever I’m sitting across from.

However, like me, hair glosses are severely misunderstood. Many people fail to realize that they offer more than just a bit of shine. Celebrity hairstylist and colorist Dimitris Giannetos tells Vogue that “they also enhance color, improve softness, and help seal the cuticle for a smooth finish.” When choosing a gloss, he recommends looking for a formula that hydrates and boosts vibrancy, leaving hair looking healthier, softer, and more radiant in mere minutes. And these days, plenty of formulas go beyond simply making hair look good, with ingredients that help improve the condition of the hair itself, too.
points: The best hair gloss treatments can restore shine in minutes, all from the comfort of your home.

articles.title: Firefox Can Now Block Ads on iOS (but You Have to Enable It)
articles.summary: Firefox users on iOS can now get rid of a lot of ad noise when browsing on their mobile device. Mozilla is slowly rolling out native ad blocking, which you can enable once the tool is available on your account.
body: According to Mozilla's support page detailing the new feature, Firefox will block third-party ad networks and exchanges along with many third-party ads served on websites at the network level. It will also block ad-related trackers, pop-ups, and overlays. The platform is still letting some ads through, though: For example, you'll still see ads in search results from engines like Google, Bing, and DuckDuckGo, as well as sponsored content on the Firefox Home and New Tab pages. There may also be ads that aren't covered by the EasyList filter list.

Ad blocking in Firefox will be off by default. To enable it, open the iOS app, tap the three dots, and go to Settings > Browsing. Under the Content header, toggle on Ad Blocker. You can do this from the Site menu by tapping Ad Blocker (underneath the site name and URL), which will open the Browsing menu directly. The site menu will show you at a glance whether ad blocking is on or off.
Firefox says this feature is currently "experimental," meaning it hasn't yet been made available to all users, so you may not see these options in your browser settings.
points: Firefox users on iOS can now get rid of a lot of ad noise when browsing on their mobile device.
Mozilla is slowly rolling out native ad blocking, which you can enable once the tool is available on your account.

articles.title: Ahead of TV’s Biggest Night, Stars Gathered for the HBO Max Emmy Nominee Celebration Luncheon
articles.summary: This past weekend, the silver screen’s leading names donned their finest brunch attire to celebrate one another ahead of the 78th annual Primetime Emmy Awards on September 14.
body: Hargitay, who’s readying to host the ceremony at the Peacock Theater next month, was the first to arrive. Her upcoming gig sees her as the first woman to emcee the event in 15 years. “I’m going to be hosting for the next five years to make that up,” Hargitay laughed to Vogue with a wink. “It’s crazy that a woman hasn’t hosted in such a long time, but that’s changing. I’m pretty sure in the future there’s going to be a lot more women hosts because there are so many incredibly funny and talented women that would kill it as hosts.”

Hargitay is no stranger to the Emmys. Having starred as Captain Olivia Benson on SVU since 1999, she has earned eight nominations and won for lead drama actress in 2006. This year, she’s a double nominee for her deeply personal HBO documentary, My Mom Jayne, which chronicles the life of her mother, actress Jayne Mansfield. “It has been one of the most meaningful and extraordinary experiences of my life because it gave me the chance to heal my family and to honor my mother and her legacy,” she said. “And to know her in a completely new way that’s full of compassion, empathy, and love.”

articles.title: NYC’s Best Bars, From Haute Hotel Lobbies to Intimate Listening Rooms
articles.summary: Above all else, New York is a drinking town. Here's where locals go for a tipple.
body: Ask 10 New Yorkers to name their favorite bar, and you’re likely to hear at least as many answers—few debates are more heated than which bar is the best in New York City.

That’s because, on any given night, a thousand versions of New York are unfolding at once: Artsy types are listening to a jazz trio in Bed-Stuy, while across the river, a group of friends is deciding which bottle of Pet Nat to split in Chinatown. A couple is ordering their second round of date night martinis at a swanky cocktail bar in the West Village, while Japanese whisky cocktails are poured over hand-chipped ice in Greenpoint.

There’s a compelling case to be made that NYC is the best bar city in the world—a place where a million people could be having entirely different nights, but still feel the same connective electric hum.

With a list of bars at least as long as the Empire State Building is tall, narrowing the options down is no small task. That’s why we scoured the city for you to find its most exciting destination for drinks right now. Below, our favorite bars in New York City.
